# Report information

A **one-page overview** of the experiment, written for the biologist rather than
the mass spectrometrist. It answers four questions: how many MHC ligands each
sample gave, whether their lengths look like an MHC-bound peptidome, how each
sample scores on the HowMaHiCo quality score, and what (if anything) deserves a
closer look. Every section points to the focused report that goes into detail.

`r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`

**Sample Set:** `r params$SampleSet`

**Data Analysis: ** `r params$DataAnalysisNames`

**Date:**  `r Sys.Date()`

**Code version:** `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")`

```{r child = system.file("rmarkdown", "shared", "setup.Rmd", package = "HowMaHiCo")}
```

```{r overview-data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
window_label <- paste0(shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " AAs")

qc_samples <- qc_samples_from_annotation(
  file.path(params$FolderDocumentation, params$AnnotationFile), params$QCColumn)
threshold_mode <- if (params$ThresholdMode == "qc_relative" && length(qc_samples) > 0)
  "qc_relative" else "default"
if (params$ThresholdMode == "qc_relative" && length(qc_samples) == 0)
  warning("ThresholdMode = 'qc_relative' but no QC samples were found; using default thresholds.")

scores <- score_sample_quality(pep_all, shortpep_range = shortpep_range,
                               mhcclass = params$MHCclass,
                               qc_samples = qc_samples,
                               threshold_mode = threshold_mode)
thresholds_used <- if (threshold_mode == "qc_relative")
  calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(qc_metrics_by_sample(pep_all, shortpep_range, params$MHCclass),
                               qc_samples,
                               thresholds = quality_thresholds_default(params$MHCclass)) else
  quality_thresholds_default(params$MHCclass)

red_flags <- overview_red_flags(scores, thresholds_used, pep_all = pep_all)
```

# At a glance

```{r at-a-glance, echo=FALSE}
n_cat <- table(factor(as.character(scores$category), levels = c("Pass", "Warning", "Fail")))
data.frame(
  Item = c("Samples", "Conditions", "Unique peptides (all lengths)",
           paste0("Unique peptides (", window_label, ")"),
           "Source proteins", "Median quality score (0-100)",
           "Samples Pass / Warning / Fail", "Red flags (High / Medium / Low)"),
  Value = c(length(samples),
            paste0(n_conditions, " (", paste(conditions, collapse = ", "), ")"),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(pep_all$Peptide), big.mark = ","),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(pep_short$Peptide), big.mark = ","),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(pep_all$Accession), big.mark = ","),
            format(stats::median(scores$composite_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
            paste(n_cat, collapse = " / "),
            paste(table(red_flags$Severity), collapse = " / "))
) |>
  kable(col.names = NULL) |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

# How many ligands per sample

Unique peptides identified in each sample, split into those inside the expected
ligand-length window for `r params$MHCclass` (`r window_label`) and all others.
A good MHC pulldown puts most of its peptides inside the window; replicates of
the same Condition should give similar totals.

```{r plot-ligands-per-sample, echo=FALSE, fig.height=3.5, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
counts_sample <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pep_all |>
    dplyr::group_by(Condition, BioReplicate, Sample) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_Peptides = dplyr::n_distinct(Peptide), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(Length_range = "All peptides"),
  pep_all |>
    dplyr::group_by(Condition, BioReplicate, Sample, Length_range) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_Peptides = dplyr::n_distinct(Peptide), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(Length_range = as.character(Length_range))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Length_range = factor(Length_range,
                                      levels = c("All peptides", "others", window_label)))
lim_sample <- ceiling(max(counts_sample$n_Peptides) * 1.2 / 100) * 100
p_ligands_per_sample <- plot_bp_count_length(counts_sample, level = "Peptides",
                                             lim_level = lim_sample,
                                             shortpep_range = shortpep_range,
                                             x_var = "Sample", palette = shortpep_colors)
ggprint_rawr(p_ligands_per_sample, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

*More detail:* `01_id_counts` (counts per Condition, BioReplicate and Sample,
by length and charge) and `02_overlaps` (how many ligands the replicates and
Conditions share).

# Do the lengths look like MHC ligands?

Length distribution of the unique peptides per Condition. MHC class I ligands
pile up at 8-11 amino acids, usually with a sharp 9-mer peak. MHC class II
ligands are longer and spread more widely, typically 13-17 amino acids. A broad
or long-tailed distribution suggests non-MHC background, such as tryptic or
degradation peptides.

```{r plot-length, echo=FALSE, fig.height=3.5, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
pep_all_unique <- pep_all |>
  dplyr::select(Peptide, Sequence, Condition, Length) |>
  unique()
p_length_overview <- plot_peplength_hist(pep_all_unique, shortpep_range = shortpep_range,
                                         type = "density", palette = shortpep_colors)
ggprint_rawr(p_length_overview, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

*More detail:* `01_id_counts` (lengths, masses, sequence motifs) and
`07_pepchem` (amino-acid composition and physicochemical properties).

# How MHC is each sample? The quality score

Each sample gets a score from 0 to 100 for how closely it resembles a genuine
MHC immunopeptidome. The score combines length-window fidelity, motif clarity,
low tryptic background, plausible charge states and, where available, mass or
calibration accuracy. **Pass** (70 or more) is a typical immunopeptidome,
**Warning** (40-70) is worth a look, and **Fail** (below 40) suggests a failed
pulldown or a non-MHC sample. Threshold mode: **`r threshold_mode`**.
`r if (length(qc_samples) > 0) paste0("QC control samples (marked *): ", paste(qc_samples, collapse = ", "), ".") else ""`

```{r plot-quality, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE}
p_quality_composite <- plot_quality_composite(scores)
ggprint_rawr(p_quality_composite, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

*More detail:* `05_quality_score` (the score of every dimension, the raw
metrics, cross-class contamination and the scoring method).

# Red flags

```{r red-flags, echo=FALSE}
if (nrow(red_flags) == 0) {
  knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "**No red flags.** Every sample passes the overview checks: no low composite ",
    "score, no quality dimension past its amber threshold, no unusually shallow ",
    "sample and no Condition without biological replicates."))
} else {
  red_flags |>
    dplyr::mutate(Sample = ifelse(is.na(Sample), "(experiment)", Sample)) |>
    kable() |>
    kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

Flags are rule-based and deliberately simple. A flag is a prompt to look, not a
verdict: a low depth or borderline score can have a perfectly good biological
reason, such as a low-input or low-HLA-expressing sample.

# Where to go next

| Question | Report |
|---|---|
| How many peptides, of which lengths and charges, per Condition / replicate / sample? | `01_id_counts` |
| How reproducible are the replicates, and what do the Conditions share? | `02_overlaps` |
| Did the LC-MS run behave (retention time, ion mobility, *m/z*, score, mass error)? | `03_lcms_qc` |
| Do peptide intensities correlate between samples, and how variable are they? | `04_quant` |
| Why did a sample score the way it did? | `05_quality_score` |
| Which ligands change in abundance between Conditions? | `06_quant_stats` |
| How do the ligands differ chemically (composition, motifs, hydrophobicity)? | `07_pepchem` |
| Which source proteins do the ligands come from? | `08_prot_all` |

```{r export-results, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Always-written export: render parameters + the red-flag list
write_input_params(params, folder = FolderResults, prefix = paste(c(result_prefix, "09_overview"), collapse = "_"))
write.csv_rawr(red_flags, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)

if (params$PlotsSave) {
  ggsave_rawr(p_ligands_per_sample, "p_ligands_per_sample", folder = FolderFigures,
              width = nrow(scores) + 6, height = 10)
  ggsave_rawr(p_length_overview, "p_length_overview", folder = FolderFigures,
              width = 16, height = 8)
  ggsave_rawr(p_quality_composite, "p_quality_composite", folder = FolderFigures,
              width = nrow(scores) + 6, height = 10)
}
```
